title: Lead Software Engineer
description:
Job Description

Lead Software Engineer 

Location: Remote

As Chegg Skills engineers, our software empowers students to move from "learning" to "earning." We build the applications and systems that help students make life-changing career transitions into high-growth job opportunities. We take pride in making education accessible to motivated career switchers, and we build the technology that helps them achieve mastery and success.

In this role, you will play a leading role in a fully remote team of diverse, motivated engineers who are rethinking what education can look like. We serve thousands of students and educators every year, and your work will directly shape how those students learn and succeed.

Chegg Skills is a growing division of Chegg focused on post-collegiate learners. We are continuing to grow our engineering team to support business expansion as more students take the next step in their careers with Chegg. Join us and help scale the engineering foundation for our next phase of growth.

About The Role

We're hiring a Lead Software Engineer, Backend to own the delivery execution of a team building backend services, APIs, and distributed systems for learner-facing and operational experiences. This is a backend-first role with full-stack reach — and the team you lead has that same full-stack reach, not backend-only depth. You need enough fluency across the stack to review a frontend PR, unblock a stuck UI engineer, or make a cross-stack architecture call, not just depth in backend.

This role sits above individual technical ownership: you are accountable for the team's delivery rhythm, you proactively coach engineers before they get stuck, and you act as the technical filter between Product and the team — refining ambiguous asks before they ever reach an engineer's backlog.

What You'll Do

- Own the team's delivery rhythm and milestone execution — break major epics into milestones with clear dependencies, spot team-wide delivery risk early, and escalate with options already framed, not after deadlines slip.
- Act as the technical filter between Product/PM and the team — refine ambiguous product asks into structured technical tasks before they hit the backlog, shielding the team from scope creep and chaotic requirements.
- Proactively coach engineers on the team — pair on complex bugs and designs, and spot technical struggles before they become delivery blockers, not just when asked.
- Set and enforce the team's technical and AI-usage norms — review standards, AI code-ownership expectations, and guardrails the whole team follows, so responsible AI usage is the default rather than something you re-check on every PR.
- Review, unblock, and make architecture calls on frontend work (React/Next.js or equivalent), even where you are not hands-on daily — your team's engineers have full-stack reach, and you need to be able to lead across the stack, not just deep in backend.
- Design and build backend services and distributed systems with a focus on scalability, reliability, and maintainability, and set the technical roadmap others on the team execute.
- Build and extend GraphQL-powered APIs and workflow-driven systems that support learner-facing and operational experiences.
- Improve reliability for integration-heavy and asynchronous workflows, including retries, idempotency, error handling, and recovery paths.
- Review PRs with a systemic lens — prevent tight coupling, catch AI-generated code that duplicates existing modules, and enforce long-term maintainability over short-term velocity.
- Drive cross-squad initiatives to completion, producing artifacts (shared tooling, workflow templates, register items) that other teams adopt without reinventing them.
- Partner closely with Product, Design, Data Engineering, Platform/SRE, and Content Operations to deliver and harden high-impact workflows.
- Treat hiring, calibration input, and team-health contributions as first-class work, not something you respond to only when chased.

Required Qualifications Technical

- Most qualified candidates will likely bring 7+ years of professional software development experience building production backend systems.
- Strong backend system design experience — distributed systems, scalability, reliability patterns, and service architecture.
- Strong experience with Java/Kotlin and/or Python-based backend systems (Spring, FastAPI, Django, or similar frameworks), plus API design and GraphQL integration.
- Experience with workflow orchestration systems (Temporal, AWS Step Functions, Airflow, or similar).
- Experience debugging production issues end to end, from symptom to root cause, fix, and prevention.
- Experience working on async or integration-heavy systems, including retries, timeouts, idempotency, and workflow/state handling.
- Strong testing and release-validation discipline in environments where engineers own quality directly.
- Experience with observability and operational ownership, including dashboards, alerts, runbooks, and participation in on-call support.
- Comfort using AI-assisted development tools responsibly, with the ability to explain, validate, and safely ship the code you produce.
- Enough exposure to React/Next.js or frontend web applications to review, unblock, or make architecture calls on frontend work — not necessarily hands-on daily, but enough to lead engineers who have full-stack reach.

Leadership & Scope

- Has owned a team's delivery rhythm — breaking epics into milestones, spotting cross-team delivery risk weeks before it becomes a miss — not just their own workstream.
- Has coached or mentored engineers with a concrete, named outcome (a promotion, a specific skill gap closed), not generic "mentored juniors" language.
- Has reviewed, unblocked, or made architecture decisions on frontend/web work, or has managed engineers who were themselves frontend or full-stack.
- Has acted as the technical filter between Product/PM and an engineering team — refining ambiguous requirements before they reached engineers.
- Has driven cross-squad initiatives to completion, producing artifacts (shared tooling, workflow templates, register items) that other teams adopted without reinventing them.
- Has set or enforced team-wide technical or AI-usage norms — review standards, AI code-ownership expectations — not just personal practice.

Tech Stack

- Backend: Python (FastAPI / Django), GraphQL, Kotlin / Java, Spring-based services, Temporal
- Frontend: React / Next.js, Node.js, Auth0-integrated web flows
- Cloud / Delivery: AWS, Docker, GitLab CI
- Observability / Operations: New Relic, Rootly, Playwright
- AI / ML: OpenAI, AWS Bedrockk

Why do we exist?

Students are working harder than ever before to stabilize their future. Our recent research study called State of the Student shows that nearly 3 out of 4 students are working to support themselves through college and 1 in 3 students feel pressure to spend more than they can afford. We founded our business on provided affordable textbook rental options to address these issues. Since then, we’ve expanded our offerings to supplement many facets of higher educational learning through Chegg Study, Chegg Math, Chegg Writing, Chegg Internships, Chegg Skills, and more to support students beyond their college experience. These offerings lower financial concerns for students by modernizing their learning experience. We exist so students everywhere have a smarter, faster, more affordable way to student.

title: Fullstack Engineer - ETS
description:
Summary
At Apple, we rely on our employees diverse set of backgrounds and perspectives to champion innovation through extraordinary ideas to surprise and delight our customers. These ideas can come from anywhere. Will that next phenomenal idea come from you?

Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.”

Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? Imagine what you could do here.

Description
Build AI-powered internal platforms that ETS runs on, from the database to the UI, and make them observable in production.

Forge builds the internal platforms Apple's Enterprise Technology Services uses to plan and operate large-scale infrastructure. These platforms put decisions on shared, current data, integrate with many internal systems, and move teams onto common standards through automation. We are now building the AI-agent layer on top of them: agents that work as operational members alongside engineers, with human judgment always in the loop.

What Makes This Role Exciting
You will take real ownership early. You'll work with product owners, infrastructure teams, and engineering partners across ETS, learn how their systems fit together, and turn that into features, integrations, and automation that teams use every day. Senior engineers review your designs and help you grow toward leading design for a component. You will also help build the AI-agent layer on our platforms, in the same codebases our engineers ship to daily.

You may start closer to product or integration work, and you should be comfortable moving between the two as the work changes.

What We're Looking For
Full-stack engineers who have shipped features to production, can apply security and scalability basics in a design and explain their choices, and learn new technologies quickly.

Responsibilities
- Build and ship features for an enterprise web application, covering data model, services, APIs, and an accessible UI, and own well-scoped features through production
- Build integrations with internal systems, and automation that helps teams adopt common standards and keeps data accurate and fresh
- Help design and build agentic workflows with approvals, guardrails, and audit trails, and help evaluate how reliably they work
- Help make our data AI-ready by exposing it through well-defined interfaces that agents can use reliably
- Apply security-by-design and proven scalable patterns in your designs: authentication and authorization, least privilege, secure handling of data and secrets, and graceful failure
- Make your services observable: instrument code with metrics, logs, and traces, build dashboards and alerts, and join on-call with support from the team
- Work with partner teams to understand their problems and prototype solutions quickly, with guidance from senior engineers
- Write design documents, take feedback in design reviews, review code, and help onboard interns and new teammates

Minimum Qualifications
- B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience
- 2+ years of professional software development, including shipping features to production
- Full-stack experience: a backend language such as Java (Spring Boot or similar) and web UIs built with React or Angular
- Working knowledge of security principles (authentication and authorization, least privilege, secure data handling) and scalable patterns (stateless services, caching, asynchronous messaging, retries), and the ability to apply them in a design and explain your choices
- Solid fundamentals in data structures, design patterns, REST API design, and relational databases, with a focus on testable, maintainable code
- A record of learning new technologies quickly, working through ambiguity, and communicating clearly with teammates and stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications
- Have built an LLM- or agent-based feature, whether in production, as a prototype, or as a project, and can describe how you designed and tested it
- Observability experience: using metrics, logs, and traces to understand and troubleshoot a running service
- Python, including LLM APIs or agent frameworks
- Daily use of GenAI coding tools (Claude, Copilot, Codex) to speed up development, testing, and debugging
- Secure software practices: security design reviews, dependency and vulnerability management
- CI/CD, Docker, and cloud platforms
- Schema design and query optimization on PostgreSQL, Oracle, or MySQL
- Web accessibility (WCAG) and building accessible enterprise UIs
- Experience mentoring interns or junior engineers, or contributing to inner-source or open-source projects

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Middle Software Engineer - Backend (Platform) based in India.

We are looking for a skilled Backend Software Engineer to help build and scale a high-performance payment platform designed for online businesses. In this role, you will contribute to the development of distributed backend services, robust APIs, and reliable integrations. You will work with modern technologies and collaborate with experienced engineers in a product-driven environment. The position offers the opportunity to take ownership of technical solutions, influence architectural decisions, and contribute to a growing product. You will also integrate AI-assisted development tools into your workflow while maintaining high engineering standards. From implementation and testing to deployment and production monitoring, your work will have a direct impact on platform reliability and performance.

Accountabilities

As part of the backend engineering team, you will develop and maintain scalable services while contributing to technical design, deployment practices, and operational excellence. You will collaborate across teams, take ownership of assigned changes, and help ensure that services remain reliable, maintainable, and compatible as the platform evolves.

- Implement backend services within high-performance, distributed systems, working with senior engineers on complex technical decisions. 
- Contribute to service architecture and API development for internal teams and external integrations, ensuring appropriate communication guarantees, idempotency, and backward compatibility. 
- Apply modern engineering practices, including test-driven and behavior-driven development where appropriate. 
- Write clean, maintainable code supported by meaningful unit and integration tests. 
- Integrate AI tools into the development workflow, critically reviewing and validating generated output. 
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams in a product-oriented environment. 
- Participate in code reviews, provide constructive feedback, and incorporate suggestions from colleagues. 
- Document service behavior, design decisions, and operational considerations. 
- Own assigned changes throughout implementation, testing, deployment, and production verification, including canary releases. 
- Build observability into services and contribute to diagnosing and resolving production incidents. 

Requirements

You bring a solid foundation in backend engineering and practical experience developing reliable services with Java and distributed systems. You are comfortable working with databases, messaging technologies, deployment pipelines, and testing practices, and you can balance independent problem-solving with effective collaboration.

- Proficiency in Java and a good understanding of backend architecture, API design, and scalability fundamentals. 
- Familiarity with distributed systems, including concurrency, error handling, and retry mechanisms. 
- Practical knowledge of PostgreSQL, including query optimization, indexing, and data modeling. 
- Understanding of microservice architecture and synchronous and asynchronous service communication, particularly with Apache Kafka.

- Practical experience writing unit and integration tests, with sound judgment about what to test and at which level. 
- Regular experience using AI-assisted development tools, including the ability to select appropriate tasks for AI and validate its output. 
- Interest in the payments industry, particularly payment routing, retries, and subscriptions, is an advantage.

title: Software Engineer -Backend
description:
- Are you curious, excited by experimentation and always looking to innovate?
- Do you want to work in embedded payments where you can keep learning and developing whilst getting hands-on experience?
- Do you want to have the opportunity to play an important role in a rapidly growing and exciting Fintech business?

If so, we would love to connect and collaborate!

Who We Are

Modulr is the payments automation platform that streamlines money movement with accuracy, control and reliability — built to scale. We process more than 200m transactions and over £180bn in payment value on an annualised basis, and we’re trusted by over 6,000 businesses from fast-growing SMEs to global enterprises.

We automate how money moves into and out of a business — payroll, supplier payments, spend management and payment collection — through a single platform, connected to the accounting and payroll systems finance teams already use and underpinned by principal memberships of Visa and Mastercard and direct access to central bank infrastructure.

As a regulated payments provider with over a decade of experience, we’re the platform finance teams trust to run mission-critical operations. Modulr is backed by PayPal, FIS, General Atlantic, Blenheim Chalcot, Frog Capital and Highland Europe, with over 400 employees across London, Edinburgh, Amsterdam, Mumbai and Pune.

The Team

At Modulr we are focused on building autonomous squads that are focused on working in

the best possible way. We operate in a tribes and squad model with each area focused on

a particular growth area. Each squad is small and cross-functional. We have big ambitions and have many interesting challenges ahead.

Summary

In this role you will design, build, and evolve the next generation of Modulr’s event-driven payments platform. You’ll work across the full engineering lifecycle—from shaping technical approaches to delivering production-grade software—within a squad that values ownership, excellence, and continuous improvement.

Specific duties

- Engineering & Architecture
- Design and develop backend services using Java (17+) or similar OO languages.
- Build and evolve microservices and distributed, event-driven components in a cloud-native environment.

- Work with relational data stores, especially PostgreSQL, and contribute to data modelling.

Distributed Systems & Reliability

- Engineer solutions for concurrency, idempotency, fault tolerance, retries, and high availability.

Quality & Testing

DevOps, Cloud & Tooling

- Use and improve deployment pipelines and operational tooling (Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, AWS services).
- Contribute to internal frameworks, shared libraries, and engineering best practices.
- Help shape the evolution of our platform toward a more flexible, modern architecture.

Collaboration & Delivery

- Work in an agile environment, contributing to planning, design discussions, and iterative delivery.
- Collaborate across squads to shape technical solutions that span multiple systems.
- Document best practices, reference architectures, and design approaches others can rely on.

About You

You’re an engineer who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and enjoys solving complex, system-level problems. You bring:

- Expertise in Java or another OO language with willingness to work in Java.
- Strong understanding of OOP, design patterns, and distributed systems fundamentals.
- Experience building and operating microservices in production.
- Ability to reason about concurrency, performance, and system behaviour under load.
- Clear, proactive communication and a collaborative, team-first mindset.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills supported by sound engineering judgement.
- Ability to manage complexity, balance competing priorities, and deliver high-quality work.
- A growth mindset—you enjoy learning, improving, and helping others grow.
- A self-starter attitude with a passion for ownership and continuous improvement.

ModInclusion

title: SDE-2 Backend
description:
Job Title: SDE - 2 Backend
Location: Bangalore (On-site; full-time)

About Locus
Battle-tested in 350+ deployments across 30+ countries, Locus is an agentic Transportation Management System for all-mile, all-channel, trusted by enterprises like Unilever, Nestlé, and Siam Makro.
The platform unifies orders, capacity, and carrier networks into one living plan, aligning planning, execution, and settlement so promises become proof. AI co-pilots with guardrails surface risk early and recommend the next best move to protect SLAs and reduce empty miles.
In 2025, Locus joined the Ingka Group (IKEA Retail) family, marking a major milestone in our journey. Backed by the scale and strength of IKEA, we continue to operate independently while accelerating our mission to make global supply chains faster, smarter, and more sustainable.

Our Journey and Impact
Since 2015, Locus has been on a mission to make logistics decision-making intelligent, sustainable, and real-world ready. Our platform has powered billions of deliveries across 30+ countries for global enterprises, driving measurable impact in cost savings, carbon reduction, and SLA performance. With the strength of the IKEA ecosystem behind us, we’re scaling that impact even further.

Our Global Footprint
Headquartered in Bangalore, with teams across the U.S., U.K., UAE, and Southeast Asia, Locus brings together 170+ engineers, designers, and problem-solvers united by a single goal: to reinvent how the world moves goods.

Traits We Value
We look for people who are:
● Global in mindset: curious about diverse markets and ideas.
● Unrelenting in drive: energized by complex challenges.
● Intelligent in approach: analytical, creative, and thoughtful.
● Dynamic in execution: adaptive and decisive in fast-moving contexts.
● Exact in craft: detail-oriented and committed to excellence.

Role Overview
As an SDE 2 Backend Engineer at Locus, you will design, build and deliver backend systems across a mix of client and internal projects. You’ll own your work from scoping to production and make sure it stays reliable, secure and fast after it ships. Based on project needs, you will be allocated to one of the tracks below, and you may move between them over time. Engineers here build with AI tools every day, and we expect you to use them to its full potential.
Project Tracks
- Managed Services: Own a Locus service end to end for enterprise clients. You’ll build new services and enhancements from the ground up, and you’ll maintain it in production. Maintenance includes on-call support, root-cause analysis and configuration changes.
- Agentic Development: Build AI agent–based solutions that automate decisions and workflows, for clients and for Locus teams.
- Custom Integrations: Build and maintain integrations between Locus and client or third-party systems. This means APIs, data mapping and reliable message handling.

Key Responsibilities
- Project Delivery: Understand requirements from clients or internal teams, scope the work, estimate it, and deliver it on time and with quality.
- System Design: Design scalable backend services and APIs with low latency and high throughput.
- Core Development: Build, test and deploy new features and enhancements in Java, keeping the code clean and maintainable.
- Integration: Connect Locus with client and third-party systems, and with our frontend and data teams.
- Production Support: Investigate and fix production issues, find the root cause, and prevent repeats.
- On-Call: Depending on the project, take part in an on-call rotation for production support.
- Performance Optimization: Find and fix bottlenecks to improve performance and scalability.
- Database Management: Design, query and maintain relational and NoSQL databases, keeping data consistent and available.
- Ownership: Own assigned work end to end, from requirements to deployment and monitoring.
- Security: Apply secure coding practices to protect systems and data.
- Code Reviews: Review peers’ code to keep standards high and share knowledge.
- Mentorship: Guide junior engineers and foster a culture of learning and innovation.

Skills and Qualifications
- Core Expertise: Proficiency in Java and frameworks like Spring Boot.
- AI-Assisted Development: Proficiency in using AI tools to design, write, test and debug code, with the judgement to review AI output and take responsibility for it.
- Good to have: Node.js and React
- Database Knowledge: Experience with MySQL, PostgreSQL or similar, and hands-on knowledge of NoSQL solutions like MongoDB or Cassandra.
- Cloud Experience: Familiarity with AWS, Azure or GCP for deployment and infrastructure management.
- Tooling: Experience with CI/CD pipelines, Git, and monitoring and observability tools (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana).
- Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills, with a focus on algorithms, data structures and system design.
- Collaboration: Ability to work closely with cross-functional teams and adapt to a fast-paced environment.
- Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field.

What We Offer
Join Locus and become part of a visionary team that is redefining logistics through innovation and smart distribution. We provide competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a collaborative environment where your expertise will drive both your growth and that of the organization.

Locus is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Equifax is transforming how global credit, data, and analytics platforms are engineered. Based in our Trivandrum Technology Hub and reporting to a Senior Software Engineer, the Software Engineer (Full Life Cycle) is Equifax’s core individual contributor engineering role building, testing, deploying, and operating software and AI-native systems end-to-end with no separate QA handoff. Quality, security, compliance, and technical documentation are owned directly by you as the engineer writing the code, enforced through automated testing, quality gates, and AI-assisted validation embedded in the CI/CD pipeline. You will also apply Context Engineering practices building prompt workflows, integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, and implementing hallucination guardrails in production applications.

What You’ll Do

- End-to-End Full Life Cycle Execution: Design, develop, test, deploy, and operate reliable, scalable microservices and cloud-native features end-to-end without downstream QA, SDET, or Technical Writing handoffs. 
- Embedded Quality, Security & Compliance: Write comprehensive automated test suites (unit, integration, contract, and API tests) and enforce security, compliance, and code quality standards directly through CI/CD quality gates and AI-assisted validation. 
- Applied AI & Context Engineering: Implement prompt engineering patterns, integrate RAG pipelines, manage knowledge base context payloads, and build hallucination-prevention guardrails into production services. 
- Cloud-Native Development & Operations: Build and maintain containerized services on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), troubleshoot production issues, analyze root causes, and ensure high service availability. 
- Technical Documentation & Agile Collaboration: Maintain clear, up-to-date technical documentation as code alongside your services and collaborate actively in sprint planning, code reviews, and retrospectives within a globally distributed engineering team. 

What Experience You Need

- Experience & Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/Engineering (or equivalent practical experience) with 4-6 years of hands-on software engineering experience building production web applications or distributed microservices. 
- Core Backend & Full-Stack Development: 3+ years of hands-on experience writing, debugging, and optimizing production code in Modern Java (JDK 17+), Spring Boot, and TypeScript/JavaScript. 
- Cloud & Container Fundamentals: 2+ years of hands-on experience developing and deploying cloud-native applications on GCP (or AWS/Azure) utilizing Kubernetes (GKE/EKS) and Docker. 
- Automated Testing & CI/CD Ownership: Demonstrated experience owning code quality end-to-end using automated testing frameworks (e.g., JUnit, Mockito, WireMock, RestAssured) and working with CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins/GitHub Actions), Helm Charts, and Terraform. 
- Context Engineering & LLM Integration: Practical experience integrating LLMs into software workflows specifically building or consuming RAG pipelines, structuring prompts/context windows, and validating AI outputs for accuracy and safety. 

What Could Set You Apart

- GCP Data & Messaging Ecosystem: Hands-on experience working with Pub/Sub, BigQuery, Dataflow (Apache Beam), Bigtable, GCS, or Cloud Composer (Airflow). 
- Frontend Web Development: Experience developing responsive UI components using Angular 
- Database & Modern Build Tooling: Proficiency with relational/NoSQL databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Cloud SQL) and modern build/version control tools (Maven, Gradle, Git). 
- Regulated Domain Experience: Prior experience building secure, compliant software within FinTech, banking, credit, or data-intensive enterprise environments.

title: Product Engineering Lead
description:
Manifest Global empowers in building companies that connect the world towards growth, prosperity, and innovation. Our portfolio includes trailblazer brands such as Cialfo, BridgeU, Explore, Kaaiser, EduGo, and Flow AI and which are dedicated to expanding global student mobility by serving their respective stakeholders in the ecosystem.

Our Mission

To create a world where every student, regardless of their ethnicity, nationality, socio-economic status, and learning preference, gets equal access to higher education through our world-class network of portfolio brands; a network that globally connects community stakeholders that provide the finest resources and support material, anywhere in the world and at any time.

Manifest Global:

What This Role Is

Every year, millions of students make a decision that sets the direction of their lives: where to study, what to study, and which country they will build a career in. That decision runs through a counselor's office, a university's admissions funnel, a family's conversation with an advisor, and a visa timeline — and almost none of the signal from one step reaches the next. Manifest exists to connect that journey, and it does it through products that each serve one part of it exceptionally well.

This role owns one of those parts at a time. As a Product Engineering Lead, you take full technical ownership of a single business platform, accountable for one thing above all: making the user that platform serves successful at what they are trying to do. You go deep on that user — their workflow, their friction, what "success" actually means for them — and you build the product that delivers it.

This is a hands-on individual contributor seat. The engineers building on your platform report to you — none or a handful today, growing as the platform does. Your leverage comes from how completely you understand one stakeholder, how good the product you build for them becomes, and how well you bring the rest of the business along with you.

You report to the Engineering Ma nager. You are assessed on two things: the delivery of the platform you're leading and the product-outcome metrics aligned to it — the measures of whether the user you serve is genuinely more successful. Both move together, and both are how your performance is judged.

You do this inside a larger system. Manifest is several products becoming one connected whole, with a shared intelligence layer running underneath. You don't own that layer or the architecture that spans the platforms — but you understand the portfolio deeply, you know how your platform connects to the others, and you build in a way that draws on the shared layer and feeds signal back into it. Your focus is narrow by design. Your awareness of the whole is not.

One thing you do not do is build your own plumbing. Auth, notifications, reporting and integrations come from the shared layer. Infrastructure and quality come from their own lines. Your accountability is for using them rather than quietly working around them.

How the Role Grows

You own one platform, and you own it for as long as it is yours to build. Growth here is not a move sideways — it is the platform getting bigger underneath you. The seat starts at one engineer or none, and as the platform earns investment, engineers are added under you rather than beside you; the model is deliberately built so that going from one person to five needs the lead to have grown into it, not a new manager above it. Past that there is a real choice rather than a ladder. Some people go deeper on the IC track toward staff, where the scope stops being one platform and becomes the systems every platform is built on. Others find they want the wider org and move toward engineering management. We would rather you choose honestly than default. The one thing not on the table is drifting out of the code.

What Makes This Role Different

Most lead engineer roles ask you to work through a backlog. This one asks you to own an outcome for a specific user and build whatever it takes to get there — including the quality of it and what happens to it in production, and including the AI-native product that user has never had before.

The leverage is the Manifest ecosystem. You are not building for your user from scratch and in isolation. You have a shared intelligence layer to build on, signal from across the portfolio to draw on, and a company that is AI-native from first principles. That means you can build recommendations, workflows, and agentic experiences for your platform that a standalone product in that space could never see well enough to build.

The timing is the argument. Across Manifest's platforms, AI is at the point where it stops being a feature and becomes the way the product works. The person who defines that for a given user, now, sets the direction for years.

What's Hard — And Why It's Worth It

The best engineers we know are drawn to the hard version of a problem, not the safe one. So here's the honest shape of it.

You go deep on one platform — often as its only engineer — but you build on a shared layer with its own gravity and other platforms pulling on it. Getting what your user needs sometimes means making your case against someone else's, and not always winning. That friction isn't noise. It's what forces the sharpest thinking you'll do here, and the lead who learns to fight for their user while strengthening the whole becomes the rarest kind of operator this company has.

The business leader who runs your platform knows their market cold and has their own conviction about the roadmap. Sometimes your data will say they're wrong. The moment you tell them that — in the language of their own business — and come out with their trust intact is the moment you stop being an engineer who executes and become one leaders actually follow.

And depending on the platform, you may inherit it mid-stride: someone else's half-built roadmap, live commitments, a team already in motion. Deciding what to keep, what to kill, and what to reimagine — without burning the trust that came before you — is its own skill, and one most engineers reach this level without ever having had to learn.

None of this is the easy version of a lead engineer job. That's exactly the point.

What You Own

What you decide alone

These calls are yours. No review, no approval step, no committee.

- The stack and the design inside your platform's boundary. Libraries, patterns, schema, internal structure — anything that does not cross the edge of your platform is your call to make and your call to live with.
- What ships and what gets cut, technically. Inside an agreed commitment, you decide what goes in, what slips and what is not worth building. You are not asked to justify a technical trade-off that stays inside your boundary.
- Who joins your platform. You run the loop and you make the hire. The Engineering Manager and the SVP of Engineering advise; they do not approve.
- Where your platform is agent-native, the agent's boundaries. What it can reach, what it must not, what tools it holds and what it does when it is wrong. Within the written standards, not by asking permission each time.

What goes to review

So the line is clear in both directions.

- Anything that crosses your platform's edge — a shared data model, an integration contract, an auth approach that other platforms inherit — goes through the architecture review path. That is a decision record, not an approval queue.
- A commitment date moving is a conversation with the Engineering Manager and the business owner, not a unilateral call.
- Building your own version of something the shared layer already provides. If the shared layer genuinely does not fit, make that case openly — what is not available to you is routing around it quietly.

The platform, technically

- Architecture within your platform, the codebase, the quality of what ships, and the technical debt you take on or pay down deliberately
- The design calls that sit inside your boundary — and knowing which ones are bigger than you and belong in architecture review
- Where your platform is agent-native: the agent design. What the agent does, what tools it holds, where it must not go, and how you know when it is wrong

Delivery

- What goes out, when, and what gets cut — agreed with the Engineering Manager and the business owner, decided by you technically
- A rhythm the business can plan against: commitments met, or renegotiated early rather than missed late

The people on it

- The engineers building on your platform report to you, and that grows as the platform does
- Their technical direction and the standard of what they ship

The relationship with the craft lines

- Pulling auth, notifications, reporting and integrations from Manifest Intelligence rather than building your own
- Working with infrastructure on how your platform runs, and with QE on how it is tested
- Being accountable for using the shared layer, and for saying clearly when it genuinely does not fit

Production

- Your platform's incidents, performance and customer-facing defects, with support from infrastructure
- Being the first responder for your platform rather than escalating by default

Writing it down

- Decisions of system-wide consequence go through the architecture review path, not into your head
- Enough documentation that the next person to hold this platform can see why each call was made

What Success Looks Like

The markers below are directional — we will calibrate specifics once you are in the seat.

In your first month you produce a written account of the platform as it actually is: what it does, what it depends on, where it is fragile, and what is being worked around. Where there is no codebase yet, the equivalent is a build plan agreed with the business owner that someone could actually execute.

By sixty days you have made one commitment and met it end to end, and your dependencies on the shared layer and infrastructure are named and agreed rather than assumed.

By ninety days there is a roadmap the business owner recognises as theirs, a working relationship with the architecture review path, and at least one thing your platform used to do privately now coming from Manifest Intelligence.

Over a year, technical questions about your platform stop being routed to engineering leadership, incidents have a first responder who is not the SVP, and the platform ships on a rhythm the business can plan against. And the decisions behind it are written down, so the next engineer on the platform can see why it looks the way it does.

What You Bring

You have spent six years or more building production systems, with real depth in at least one of our stacks — Rails, services, or agent and LLM systems.

You have owned a product or service end to end, including what broke in production at two in the morning. You know what it costs to be the person who gets called, and you do not confuse shipping with being done.

You are comfortable being the only engineer on something, and comfortable not staying that way. The first is about self-direction; the second is about actually wanting to grow other people rather than remaining the hero.

You make a call and write down why. Most of what goes wrong on a one-person platform is an undocumented decision that nobody can reconstruct six months later.

You work well with people who do not report to you. The craft lines are how this role gets leverage, and they respond to the engineer who comes with a clear problem rather than a demand.

You can hold your own with a business leader. You can tell them the roadmap should change, say why in the terms of their business rather than yours, and come out with their trust intact.

You are AI-native, or visibly becoming it. You have built agentic or AI-powered product into a real user workflow — something people came to rely on, not something they tried once — and you know where AI does not belong as clearly as where it does. And you are comfortable starting a codebase from nothing, or picking one up mid-flight.

You are comfortable in a distributed team across time zones — ours sits across Delhi, Pakistan, Singapore

Most importantly: you read this and your first reaction was not "this is a solid lead engineer job." It was "I want one thing that is mine, end to end, and I want to be the reason it is good."

Why Manifest

Manifest Global is building the infrastructure for global human capital mobility, connecting students, schools, universities, and employers across 150+ countries. Our portfolio spans Cialfo (AI-powered college counseling, 2,000+ schools), BridgeU (university guidance for international schools globally), Kaaiser (trusted study abroad counseling since 1997 across India and Southeast Asia), Explore (AI-powered university outreach, 1,000+ university partners), and EduGo (study abroad counseling and student placement). Together, we move talent across borders at scale. $700B flows annually in remittances from migrant workers. 85M workers will be missing from developed economies by 2030. We're building the operating system that changes that. $76M raised. Still early.

Every platform here serves one part of a student's journey. This seat is where one of those parts either works or does not.

* Implement dynamic forms, document upload workflows, status-tracking, and approval processes.

Backend Engineering

* Design and develop scalable REST APIs and microservices.

* Build integrations with external enterprise and government systems.

DevOps & Cloud-Native Deployment

* Containerize applications using Docker.
* Deploy and manage services on Kubernetes/OpenShift.
* Configure CI/CD pipelines and automate build, test, and deployment processes.
* Implement monitoring, logging, autoscaling, and high-availability configurations.

Required Skills

* 4+ years of software engineering experience in full-stack or backend development.
* Strong experience with **Python (FastAPI, Flask, Django)** and/or **TypeScript**.
* Hands-on expertise with **React.js** and **Next.js**.
* Strong understanding of **REST APIs**, microservices, and distributed systems.
* Experience with **PostgreSQL** and relational database design.
* Hands-on experience with **Docker** and **Kubernetes/OpenShift**.
* Knowledge of **Git**, CI/CD pipelines, and software development best practices.
* Strong debugging, troubleshooting, and performance optimization skills.

Preferred Skills

* Experience with **Kafka, RabbitMQ, Celery, or Redis-based messaging systems**.
* Experience building **event-driven architectures**.
* Knowledge of **OAuth2, OpenID Connect (OIDC), JWT, and RBAC**.
* Exposure to **AI/LLM integrations** and workflow automation.
* Experience with **API Gateways** and enterprise platform integrations.
* Familiarity with **Helm, Terraform, Ansible**, and Infrastructure as Code.
* Experience handling sensitive customer or citizen data.
* Experience building bilingual or multilingual applications.

* Experience with backend API development
* MySql, MongoDB and experience designing and maintaining databases
* Proven experience as a Software Engineer or similar role

description:
Bangalore, Karnātaka, India IT Ref ID: JR-024020

**Our Mission**

At Palo Alto Networks®, we’re united by a shared mission—to protect our digital way of life. We thrive at the intersection of innovation and impact, solving real-world problems with cutting-edge technology and bold thinking. Here, everyone has a voice, and every idea counts. In order to be the cybersecurity partner of choice, we must trailblaze the path and shape the future of our industry. This is something our employees work at each day and is defined by our values: Disruption, Collaboration, Execution, Integrity, and Inclusion. We weave AI into the fabric of everything we do and use it to augment the impact every individual can have. If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!

We believe collaboration thrives in person. That’s why most of our teams work from the office full time, with flexibility when it’s needed. This model supports real-time problem-solving, stronger relationships, and the kind of precision that drives great outcomes.

**Job Summary**

**About the Role**

We are looking for a Staff AI Engineer to be the technical anchor for Agentic AI in IT Quality Engineering – setting the architecture, standards and roadmap for custom Agentic AI applications across an Enterprise IT landscape spanning Salesforce, SAP, custom Licensing and Entitlement management applications, and AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning and ITSM platforms. You will decide how agents plan, act, retrieve context and hand back to a human across these systems; how they are evaluated, governed and operated in production; and how the wider engineering team builds them well. This is a hands-on role: you will still design and write the hardest parts yourself.

At Palo Alto Networks we are moving towards an AI-First engineering culture. You will shape the direction of our own internal AI platform tools for test generation, automation scripting, execution and quality reporting, and lead the engineers who build on them.

  
  

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

  
  

**Architecture & Technical Direction**

**Agentic Architecture:** Define the reference architecture for agentic systems across the landscape — planner-executor orchestration, multi-agent coordination, state, memory and recovery — and choose frameworks such as LangGraph, ADK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen or CrewAI on evidence rather than fashion.

**Event-Driven Enterprise Integration:** Architect event-driven pipelines that connect Salesforce (Platform Events, Change Data Capture, Apex, Flows), SAP (OData/BAPI services and business-object events) and custom Licensing, Entitlement, AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning and ITSM applications to AI processing with production OAuth2 lifecycle, least-privilege access and idempotent writes to systems of record.

**Context & Knowledge Architecture:** Set the retrieval strategy across the estate — vector and graph stores (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate or Milvus; Apache AGE or Neo4j), advanced topologies (Graph RAG, Corrective RAG, HyDE, agentic retrieval), and the ingestion, freshness and access-control rules that keep context correct.

**Tool & Protocol Standards:** Own the standards for tool definitions, JSON function schemas and MCP servers across teams, so that agent tool calls are schema-validated, auditable and traceable back to Jira.

**Model Strategy:** Decide when prompting and retrieval are enough and when model customisation is justified — and lead resource-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) where it is.

**Quality, Safety & Governance at Scale**

**Evaluation Strategy & Release Gates:** Define how AI agents — ours and the ones other teams build that the business depends on — are evaluated before release: golden sets, calibrated LLM-as-judge, adversarial testing, and risk-tiered release gates that block what should be blocked.

**Autonomy & HITL Governance:** Set the autonomy model — which decisions an agent may take alone, which need human approval, and how that changes as evidence accumulates — and make sure it is enforced in code, especially where agents write to systems of record.

**LLMOps & Platform Reliability:** Architect secure AI gateways, token-budget and rate-limit controls, model deployment pipelines, drift monitoring and automated rollback; own service levels, cost and incident response for production agents.

**Responsible AI & Data Governance:** Partner with security and data-governance owners to define guardrails on intellectual property and data privacy — managed secrets, explicit opt-in for any step that sends content to an external service, and an audit trail a reviewer can follow.

**Leadership & Influence**

**Design & Review Board:** Lead design reviews for agentic and AI-integrated systems across Salesforce, SAP and custom platforms, and set the code and design standards for both human-written and AI-generated code.

**Roadmap & Strategy:** Partner with engineering leadership, QE leads, product managers and enterprise architects to turn quality and business goals into a sequenced AI engineering roadmap — and say plainly what will not work.

**Mentorship & Capability Building:** Mentor Senior AI Engineers and AI Engineers, grow the next AI Architects, and shape the reference implementations and training that move engineers up our AI capability ladder.

**Cross-Organisation Influence:** Represent IT Quality Engineering in enterprise architecture and AI governance forums, and drive adoption of AI-native engineering practice beyond your own team.

**Qualifications**

**Required Skills & Experience**

  
  

**Experience:** 7–10 years of professional software engineering experience, including 3+ years in applied AI/ML, of which at least 2 years building LLM-based or agentic systems that reached production.

**Leadership Track Record:** 2+ years as a technical lead, staff engineer or architect driving architectural decisions and leading cross-functional technical initiatives to production.

**Programming Mastery:** Expert proficiency in Python and strong proficiency in Java or TypeScript/Node.js; excellent software design is a given.

**Agentic Systems Architecture:** You have designed and led production agentic systems — planner-executor orchestration, multi-agent coordination, state and memory, HITL control — and can explain the trade-offs you made and what you would change.

**Distributed & Event-Driven Systems:** Deep experience with microservices, event-driven architecture and message queues (e.g., Kafka, Pub/Sub), including idempotency, ordering, back-pressure and failure recovery.

**Retrieval at Scale:** You have designed production RAG systems over vector and/or graph stores, including access-controlled ingestion and measured retrieval quality.

**Evaluation & Governance:** You have established evaluation and release-gating practice for LLM systems — golden sets, LLM-as-judge calibration, adversarial and prompt-injection testing — that was adopted beyond your own team.

**Enterprise Integration:** Deep experience integrating with enterprise platforms — Salesforce, SAP or comparable CRM, ERP or ITSM systems — including OAuth2 lifecycle, safe write patterns and data-governance constraints.

**Cloud, LLMOps & CI/CD:** Strong experience with GCP/AWS/Azure, Docker and Kubernetes, CI/CD at enterprise scale, and operating AI services with observability, cost controls and rollback.

**AI-Assisted Development:** Deep fluency with tools such as Cursor, Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, and a track record of setting team practice for reviewing what they produce.

**Education:** B.E./B.Tech/M.Tech in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience).

**Preferred Qualifications**

**Model Customisation:** Hands-on fine-tuning with resource-efficient methods (LoRA/QLoRA), including data preparation and evaluation of the tuned model against its base.

**Integration Platforms:** Event-driven enterprise integration in practice — SAP business-object events and workflow triggers, Salesforce Platform Events or Change Data Capture, and middleware such as SnapLogic or MuleSoft.

**Model Context Protocol:** Designing MCP server estates used across teams — tools, resources and prompts, with versioning and access control.

**Managed AI Platforms:** Production experience with Vertex AI or an equivalent managed AI platform.

**AI Security:** Threat modelling for agentic systems — prompt injection, tool misuse, data exfiltration and red-teaming practice.

**Quality Engineering at Scale:** Architecting test automation or quality platforms (Playwright, REST Assured, Selenium or PyTest), including AI-assisted test generation or self-healing automation.

**Domain Expertise:** Deep grounding in B2B sales, Partner Relationship Management (PRM), the Quote-to-Cash lifecycle, or licensing, entitlement and provisioning flows.

**Industry Contribution:** Publications, conference talks or significant open-source contributions in agentic AI, retrieval or LLM evaluation.

**WAYS OF WORKING**

**Evidence over Assertion:** You measure before and after, you publish the number with its method attached, you say plainly when a result is inconclusive — and you hold the team's claims to the same standard.

**Curiosity with Rigour:** You enjoy new tooling but you test it before you trust it, and you know the difference between a demo and a system.

**Strategic Influence:** You change direction with evidence and clear writing rather than authority, with technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.

**High Autonomy:** You take ambiguous, cross-system problems and turn them into a plan a team can execute, and you raise risks early rather than late.

**Builder's Bias:** You would rather ship a narrow capability that works and is trusted than a broad one that only demos well — and you set that standard for the team.

**GROWTH PATH**

This role sits at the AI Architect tier of our internal AI capability ladder (AI User AI Engineer AI Architect), and you will operate there from the start: planner-executor orchestration at scale, multi-agent systems with human-in-the-loop control, event-driven integration across the enterprise IT landscape, and model customisation. From here the role grows in scope from a single programme to the AI engineering direction of IT Quality Engineering — and in the number of engineers you bring up the same ladder.

**THE TEAM**

You will be part of a growing, passionate and dynamic team, with the opportunity to work on challenging and exciting projects centred on what we believe is one of the most significant mission statements in the world. We also strive to be the most people-centric company ever — that means we are constantly working to make your experience amazing, and you are part of the team breaking the boundaries of what the workplace can be.

**Our Commitment**

We’re trailblazers that dream big, take risks, and challenge cybersecurity’s status quo. It’s simple: we can’t accomplish our mission without diverse teams innovating, together.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for all qualified individuals with a disability. If you require assistance or accommodation due to a disability or special need, please contact us at accommodations@paloaltonetworks.com.

title: SDE2 - Full Stack
description:
**About the role**  
  
We're hiring two backend-heavy full-stack engineers (SDE 2 or SDE 3) for the Cowork team at Sarvam. Cowork is the agentic side of Indus: users hand it real work, and an agent plans, uses tools and connectors, works in a cloud sandbox, and hands back files, docs and artifacts across web, Android, iOS, macOS and Windows.  
  
The role is full stack, but the centre of gravity is the backend: the BFF that every client talks to, and increasingly the agent harness behind it. You'll ship features end to end, from the API and data model through to the client screens on mobile, desktop and web.  
  
**What you'll work on**  
  
Most of your time goes into the BFF and the services around it; the rest into client work and the harness, depending on what the roadmap needs that quarter.

* **BFF (Chat Service):** design and own the APIs that web, mobile and desktop share: sessions, conversations, streaming turns, artifacts, connectors, custom and managed agents. Data modelling, migrations, auth and RBAC, pagination and search.
* **Real-time streaming:** stream LLM output, tool calls and agent events from the harness to clients over an event bus, and keep it correct under reconnects, retries and partial failures.
* **Agent harness and platform:** contribute to Panja, our agent harness: tool and MCP integrations, sandboxed execution, file and artifact flows, latency and token-cost work.
* **Clients:** build features end to end on our Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) and the Next.js web app, so a feature you design in the backend reaches users on every surface.
* **Production ownership:** observability, on-call, RCAs, and making the system faster and cheaper with numbers to back it.

**Tech stack**  
  
Python and PostgreSQL are the core; you don't need every item below on day one.

* **Backend:** Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL, OpenAPI
* **Supporting services:** Go
* **Mobile and desktop:** Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows)
* **Web:** Next.js, React, TypeScript

**What we're looking for**  
  
A strong backend engineer who has also shipped real frontend work and is happy to keep doing both.

* 3+ years (SDE 2) or 5+ years (SDE 3) building and running production backend services.
* Deep in at least one backend language; Python preferred, Go, Kotlin/JVM or TypeScript/Node also welcome.
* Solid API and data-model design: REST/streaming APIs, PostgreSQL schema design, migrations, indexing, transactions.
* Distributed-systems fundamentals: async processing, queues or event streams, idempotency, retries, failure handling.
* Production experience on Kubernetes or a similar platform, with observability you actually used to debug an incident.
* Has shipped user-facing features on at least one client platform: Android, iOS, desktop or web (React/Next.js). Kotlin/Compose experience is a plus, not a gate.
* Willing to pick up the side of the stack they know less, and to learn agent and LLM systems on the job.
* Clear written communication: design docs, PR descriptions, RCAs.

**Nice to have**

* Built on LLM APIs: tool calling, streaming, prompt caching, evals, or an agent loop of your own.
* MCP servers or clients, OAuth connector integrations, or sandboxed code execution.
* Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform, or native Android/iOS.
* Real-time systems: WebSockets/SSE, NATS, Kafka, or Temporal-style durable workflows.
* Go services, or performance and cost work with measurable before/after numbers.
* Open-source work or public writing we can read.

At AppsForBharat, we’re looking for a Frontend Engineer to work on the frontend app of our core consumer products and build fast, accessible experiences for millions of devotees worldwide.

You’ll work closely with Product and Design to improve how users discover, navigate, and transact on the web. * Experience integrating REST APIs and third-party SDKs into production applications.
* Experience using tools such as Mixpanel or Google Analytics to understand user behavior and running A/B tests to improve conversion.
* Familiarity with responsive styling, UI component systems, and tools such as Tailwind CSS or styled-components.

title: Senior Software Engineer - CPD
description:
Location : Bangalore/Pune
About Team & About Role:

As a Senior Software Engineer (SSE) in the Continuous Product Delivery (CPD) team, you will play a key role in providing long term stability and last mile delight to our customers. You will work closely with the core engineering team, product, and support org.

You will be working across Rubrik releases on our on-premise data backup & management offering, with a focus on the identity and access layer that secures it. You are expected to develop a strong understanding of our product and engineering architecture — particularly how authentication and authorization flow through the system, including our integrations with enterprise identity providers, directory services, and certificate-based trust chains.

We are seeking a highly skilled Golang developer with deep, practical experience in identity protocols (OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0) and applied cryptography/PKI. As a Software Engineer on this team, you will be responsible for designing, building, and hardening the systems that authenticate users, machines, and services across our platform — reasoning carefully about threat models, not just shipping features. You should have strong programming and troubleshooting skills, excellent design skills, and a solid understanding of distributed systems, OS fundamentals, and networking. The successful candidate will preferably have working knowledge of Active Directory and be able to work independently and as part of a team.

Responsibilities

- Design, build, and harden identity and access flows — OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0, Active Directory integrations — that sit in front of mission-critical systems.

- Own token and assertion lifecycle correctness: issuance, validation, expiry, rotation, and failure-mode handling for JWT/JWKS and SAML assertions.

- Apply strong applied-cryptography and PKI practices (X.509 certs, key rotation, TLS) to keep the auth path secure by default, not as an afterthought.

- Build and maintain reverse-proxy/HTTP-layer components (TLS termination, header handling) that front customer authentication traffic.

- Debug and resolve customer-facing identity/access issues, working with support to triage escalations quickly.

- Contribute to build/release and cross-platform packaging (Linux deb/rpm, Windows MSI) as needed.

- Maintain a small Windows companion application written in C#/.NET.

- Write and enhance end-to-end tests covering auth flows, failure modes, and edge cases (clock skew, revoked tokens, malformed assertions, etc.).

- Document known issues, workarounds, and design decisions in the team knowledge base as the team and product mature.

- Communicate clearly with product and engineering stakeholders on design tradeoffs, security posture, and escalation status.

Requirements

Must-have

- Minimum experience of at least 8 Years

- Strong hands-on programming skills in Golang.

- Deep, practical knowledge of identity protocols: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 and SAML 2.0 — including token/assertion internals, standard flows, and failure modes.

- Working knowledge of Active Directory.

- Applied cryptography/PKI experience: X.509, JWT/JWKS, key rotation, TLS.

- Strong security engineering discipline — comfortable reasoning about threat models and building software to protect mission-critical systems, not just make features work.

- Solid understanding of OS fundamentals, networking, and concurrency.

- Working knowledge of Linux; comfortable writing shell/bash scripts.

- Simple, effective written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-have

- Directory internals (schema, bind operations).

- HTTP internals and reverse proxying (TLS, header injection).

- Build/release and cross-platform packaging (Linux deb/rpm, Windows MSI).

- Secret-manager internals, Redis, Win32, policy engines.

- Basic C#/.NET (to maintain the companion app).

title: Software Engineer
description:
Location : Pune
About Team & About Role:

As a Software Engineer (SE) in the Continuous Product Delivery (CPD) team, you will play a key role in providing long term stability and last mile delight to our customers. You will work closely with the core engineering team, product, and support org.

You will be working across Rubrik releases on our on-premise data backup & management offering, with a focus on the identity and access layer that secures it. You are expected to develop a strong understanding of our product and engineering architecture — particularly how authentication and authorization flow through the system, including our integrations with enterprise identity providers, directory services, and certificate-based trust chains.

We are seeking a highly skilled Golang developer with deep, practical experience in identity protocols (OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0) and applied cryptography/PKI. As a Software Engineer on this team, you will be responsible for designing, building, and hardening the systems that authenticate users, machines, and services across our platform — reasoning carefully about threat models, not just shipping features. You should have strong programming and troubleshooting skills, excellent design skills, and a solid understanding of distributed systems, OS fundamentals, and networking. The successful candidate will preferably have working knowledge of Active Directory and be able to work independently and as part of a team.

Responsibilities

- Design, build, and harden identity and access flows — OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0, Active Directory integrations — that sit in front of mission-critical systems.

- Own token and assertion lifecycle correctness: issuance, validation, expiry, rotation, and failure-mode handling for JWT/JWKS and SAML assertions.

- Apply strong applied-cryptography and PKI practices (X.509 certs, key rotation, TLS) to keep the auth path secure by default, not as an afterthought.

- Build and maintain reverse-proxy/HTTP-layer components (TLS termination, header handling) that front customer authentication traffic.

- Debug and resolve customer-facing identity/access issues, working with support to triage escalations quickly.

- Contribute to build/release and cross-platform packaging (Linux deb/rpm, Windows MSI) as needed.

- Maintain a small Windows companion application written in C#/.NET.

- Write and enhance end-to-end tests covering auth flows, failure modes, and edge cases (clock skew, revoked tokens, malformed assertions, etc.).

- Document known issues, workarounds, and design decisions in the team knowledge base as the team and product mature.

- Communicate clearly with product and engineering stakeholders on design tradeoffs, security posture, and escalation status.

Requirements

Must-have

- Strong hands-on programming skills in Golang.

- Deep, practical knowledge of identity protocols: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 and SAML 2.0 — including token/assertion internals, standard flows, and failure modes.

- Working knowledge of Active Directory.

- Applied cryptography/PKI experience: X.509, JWT/JWKS, key rotation, TLS.

- Strong security engineering discipline — comfortable reasoning about threat models and building software to protect mission-critical systems, not just make features work.

- Solid understanding of OS fundamentals, networking, and concurrency.

- Working knowledge of Linux; comfortable writing shell/bash scripts.

- Simple, effective written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-have

- Directory internals (schema, bind operations).

- HTTP internals and reverse proxying (TLS, header injection).

- Build/release and cross-platform packaging (Linux deb/rpm, Windows MSI).

- Secret-manager internals, Redis, Win32, policy engines.

- Basic C#/.NET (to maintain the companion app).

title: Software Engineer (L2)
description:
Who we are 

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.
.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio's next Software Engineer for Stytch, where you'll shape the next generation of identity products.

About the job

This position is needed to help build and scale Stytch’s core product as we bring Stytch capabilities to Twilio’s full customer base, delivering secure, developer-first identity experiences.

Join the Stytch team at Twilio to shape the next generation of identity products. You’ll build backend systems that power authentication, authorization, and emerging agentic and non-human identity use cases. You’ll partner closely with product and engineering leadershp to design and deliver high-impact, customer-facing features, and evolve our platform for Twilio scale. This is a rare chance to operate like a startup within Twilio: you’ll work in a high-ownership environment with startup speed, backed by Twilio’s reach and scale.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

- Build backend product capabilities for Stytch’s identity platform on Twilio—shipping new API surfaces and core authentication flows, including agentic and non-human identity use cases.

- Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to set direction, translate customer needs into product capabilities, and deliver high-impact roadmap features.

- Collaborate across Twilio and Stytch teams to align on architecture, integrate platform capabilities, and unblock cross-team initiatives.

- Operate with deep technical ownership: author design docs, drive key technical decisions, review code, and stay close to the systems you ship.

- Build in ambiguity—break down complex problems, make pragmatic tradeoffs, and design developer experiences that delight our customers.

- Improve production quality and resilience through strong observability, incident response and remediation.

- Mentor and support other engineers through pairing, feedback, and knowledge-sharing, helping raise the team’s technical bar and culture.

Qualifications 

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

- 3+ years experience in designing, building and operating high-scale, mission critical cloud based production systems.

- Familiarity with a production-grade code base in a modern programming language, applying best practice coding standards and writing high quality code.

- Extensive experience with RESTful API design and development.

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or related industry experience.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Schedule: ability to work non-standard, on-call rotation weekend and holiday hours.

Desired:

- Familiarity with Go, TypeScript, and DynamoDB

- Experience building developer tools or SDKs

- Experience building and owning products consumed by paying customers

- Builder at heart. Through a hobby or your profession, you are passionate about being hands on and seeing your work come to life.

Location

This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in San Francisco, CA, Oakland, CA, San Jose, CA, or the surrounding areas.

This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in CA, CT, NJ, NY, PA, WA.

Travel 

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Compensation

*Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only.

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

- Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of San Francisco Bay area): $123,760 - $154,700.

- This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Application deadline information (required for ALL US jobs)

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until February 1st, 2026 but may change based on business needs.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure (Datastores)
location: Remote - USA, US - Remote Zone 1 (Job Requisitions Only)
description:
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase.

The Datastores team owns Coinbase's production online databases and caches: Aurora, RDS Postgres, MongoDB Atlas, DynamoDB, ElastiCache (Valkey, Redis), and ClickHouse. We build the paved paths, tooling, and client libraries that let hundreds of engineering teams run reliable, secure, cost-efficient data layers serving millions of requests per second. We are hiring a Staff Software Engineer to help evolve our storage platform: consolidating how databases are provisioned and operated, building zonal resilience and disaster recovery into every production datastore, securing access to data, and giving teams well-paved ways to use it.

What you'll do

- Shape the architecture and multi-year roadmap of Coinbase's storage platform across relational, document, key-value, and caching datastores.

- Lead platform initiatives from design through production, such as consolidating databases onto shared, proxy-fronted clusters and building client libraries that make applications resilient to failover.

- Drive resilience and disaster recovery for online datastores: zonal failover, backups and replication, restore tooling, and regular recovery validation.

- Harden the security and compliance posture of our datastores: encryption and key management, least-privilege access, audit logging, and the controls and evidence that regulators and auditors expect.

- Design for reliability, performance, and cost efficiency; set and defend SLOs, lead capacity planning, and eliminate recurring classes of incidents.

- Partner with senior engineers and product-group leadership on database technology choices, and work directly with AWS, MongoDB, and other vendors.

- Mentor engineers across the team, raise the bar on design reviews and operational excellence, and participate in the on-call rotation.

Required Skills and Experience

- 8+ years of industry experience building and operating large-scale, highly available distributed systems in production.

- Deep hands-on experience operating online databases at scale in production (e.g., PostgreSQL/Aurora, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Redis/Valkey, Memcached), including replication, failover, performance tuning, and version upgrades.

- Solid understanding of distributed database architecture, consistency models, and the trade-offs between datastore technologies.

- Experience securing data infrastructure in a regulated environment: encryption at rest and in transit, key management, access control, and audit requirements.

- Strong backend development skills in Go, Java, or Python, with a track record of building database tooling, client libraries, or automation.

- Experience leading cross-team technical initiatives, writing clear design documents, and influencing without direct authority.

- Strong communication skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

$218,025—$256,500 USD
